# Native releases

The canonical repository is `git.parano1d.org/ignotusnemo/parano1d`. GitHub `proof-native/parano1d` runs the manual Platform CI and Native Release workflows. GitHub `ignotusnemo/parano1d` and GitLab `ignotusnemo/parano1d` mirror the same source, tag, release notes and binary files.

## Prepare

- Merge the reviewed release source into canonical `main`, then synchronize `main` on `proof-native`, `origin` and `gitlab`. Keep the development branch synchronized separately.
- Set the workspace version and commit `.github/release-notes/vVERSION.md`. Keep each prose paragraph and list item on one physical line.
- Use the frozen mainnet legacy pack, v2 pack, v2 pins and two legacy retirement verification keys. The v2 archive contains verification keys only; a future mainnet retirement certificate depends on the actual fork predecessor.
- Authenticate `gh` for `proof-native/parano1d`, or supply `GH_TOKEN` with access to that repository. The local publisher checks every remote's `main` before assigning a release tag.

```sh
./scripts/publish_release.sh 2.0.0 /path/to/history-step-pack-v1 \
  --v2-pack /path/to/frozen-v2-pack \
  --v2-pins /path/to/v2-pins.env \
  --retirement-keys /path/to/verification-keys \
  --channel stable
```

The publisher runs Platform CI for the exact source commit. After success it creates one annotated tag on all four remotes, opens a draft in `proof-native`, uploads both normalized packs and starts Native Release. Both workflows run only by manual dispatch; pushes and pull requests do not start CI.

## Build and publish

Native Release verifies the tag, source version, notes, successful Platform CI run, archive digests and complete archive contents. Each platform receives the same two packs and builds with `--pack`, `--v2-pack`, `--v2-pins` and `--retirement-keys`. Rust build validation checks the matrix identities and activation schedule. The transition release includes both legacy classes; do not pass `--retired-history` for the pre-fork release.

Linux x86-64, Linux ARM64, Windows x86-64, macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel each produce a Core archive and a GUI installer. The release stays a draft until all ten deliverables succeed. Publication adds the two input packs and `SHA256SUMS`, for thirteen release assets in total.

If a build fails, inspect that job before rerunning it. A changed source commit requires a new Platform CI result. Never move an already published release tag or combine assets from different release commits.

## Synchronize delivery

Download the complete published release from `proof-native` and verify every entry in `SHA256SUMS`. Copy those exact thirteen files and the committed release notes to the canonical Forgejo release and both mirrors. GitLab stores the files in its generic package registry and exposes them as release asset links. No platform rebuild is needed for mirroring.

Before considering publication complete, download the assets from each destination and compare their digests with the original manifest. Check the release title, notes, channel and annotated tag on every host as well. Automatic source-code archives generated by a hosting service are separate from the thirteen release assets.
